definition_zh: 青霉素；盘尼西林；青霉素类药物
definition_en: an antibiotic medicine obtained from a mould, used to kill bacteria and cure infections
core_image: 培养皿上那圈青绿色的霉，把周围的细菌都清空成一个透明的圆圈
scene: 实验室里，一块发霉的培养皿被放在窗边，霉菌周围的细菌全都不见了。Fleming noticed that a mould had killed the bacteria around it and called the substance penicillin.
sceneCN: 这里 penicillin 是「青霉素」（第 1 个义项：从霉菌中取得的抗生素药物）；句意：弗莱明发现一种霉菌杀死了它周围的细菌，便把这种物质称作青霉素。

pos.zh: 青霉素；盘尼西林（一种抗生素）

derivatives.zh: 由 penicillin 加酶类后缀 -ase 构成，指分解青霉素的酶
由 penicillinase 加 resistant 构成的复合形容词，指不被青霉素酶分解的
由 benzyl（苄基）加 penicillin 构成，指天然青霉素的主要成分苄青霉素

senses.title: The antibiotic itself
senses.titleCN: 青霉素；盘尼西林（抗生素）
senses.definition: an antibiotic substance produced by a mould and used to kill bacteria or stop them growing
senses.definitionCN: 由霉菌产生的抗生素物质，用于杀灭细菌或阻止细菌生长
senses.example: Penicillin was the first antibiotic in wide medical use.
senses.exampleCN: 青霉素是第一种被广泛用于医疗的抗生素。
senses.why: The word began as the name Fleming gave a substance made by a mould of the Penicillium genus, so the drug and the mould share one origin.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早是弗莱明给一种青霉菌属霉菌所产物质起的名字，所以药物与霉菌同出一源。

senses.title: The family of medicines
senses.definition: any of a group of related antibiotics, including penicillins with modified side chains
senses.definitionCN: 包括侧链经过改造的青霉素在内的、彼此相关的一类抗生素
senses.example: Some newer penicillins work against bacteria that resist the original drug.
senses.exampleCN: 一些较新的青霉素能对付抵抗原有药物的细菌。
senses.why: Once chemists altered the side chain, the single drug name became a family label for many close chemical relatives.
senses.whyCN: 化学家改造侧链之后，单个药名就成了一大类化学近亲的共同称呼。

senses.title: Fleming and the mould
senses.definition: the discovery of the drug in a mouldy culture dish, and the story attached to it
senses.definitionCN: 在发霉的培养皿中发现这种药物，以及与之相连的发现故事
senses.example: The penicillin story begins with a contaminated dish left by an open window.
senses.exampleCN: 青霉素的故事始于一只被窗边空气污染的培养皿。
senses.why: Popular history uses the word for the accidental find itself, because the mould and the cure have one name.
senses.whyCN: 大众叙事用这个词指那次偶然发现，因为霉菌与疗法共用一个名字。

senses.title: Produced and prescribed
senses.definition: the drug as something manufactured in bulk and given to patients for infections
senses.definitionCN: 作为大批量生产并用于病人感染治疗的药物
senses.example: During the war, penicillin was mass-produced for wounded soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 战时，青霉素被大量生产供受伤士兵使用。
senses.why: From a lab curiosity the word moved into factories and clinics, so it can name the product rather than the science.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从实验室奇观走进工厂与诊所，因此也能指产品而非科学发现。

intro.en: Penicillin was coined by Alexander Fleming from the scientific Latin name of the blue-green mould Penicillium notatum.
intro.cn: penicillin 由亚历山大·弗莱明根据青绿色霉菌的学名 Penicillium notatum 造出。

items.en: Pencillus means a little tail, and the mould was named for the brush-like shape of its spores.
items.cn: pencillus 意为「小尾巴」，霉菌因其孢子束呈画笔状而得名。

items.en: Mycologists formalise the genus name Penicillium from that Latin root.
items.cn: 真菌学家在这一年以该拉丁词根定下属名 Penicillium。

items.en: Alexander Fleming reports a mould that kills bacteria and calls the active substance penicillin.
items.cn: 亚历山大·弗莱明报告一种杀灭细菌的霉菌，并把活性物质称作 penicillin。

items.en: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain turn it into a purified drug, and the name becomes standard medical English.
items.cn: 霍华德·弗洛里与恩斯特·钱恩把它提纯成药物，这个词成为标准医学英语。

items.en: Factories make it in bulk and later versions add prefixes such as benzyl or phenoxymethyl.
items.cn: 工厂大批量生产，后来的变体又加上 benzyl、phenoxymethyl 等前缀。

note.en: Penicillin is the name of one antibiotic, next to other antibiotic names that share the ending -cillin.
note.cn: penicillin 是一种抗生素的名字，与同以 -cillin 结尾的抗生素名称相邻。

entries.definition: the genus of moulds from which penicillin was first obtained
entries.definitionCN: 最初取得青霉素所用的青霉菌属

entries.definition: an enzyme that breaks down penicillins
the main natural penicillin, also called penicillin G
entries.definitionCN: 主要的天然青霉素，又称青霉素 G

entries.definition: a medicine that kills bacteria or stops them growing
entries.definitionCN: 抗生素：杀灭细菌或阻止其生长的药物

entries.definition: a widely used penicillin with a modified side chain
entries.definitionCN: 侧链经过改造、广泛使用的青霉素类药

entries.definition: a substance applied to skin or wounds to kill germs
entries.definitionCN: 用于皮肤或伤口的杀菌剂

normalIntro.en: Penicillin is one word with two halves: the mould name and a chemical suffix, joined by the illness it cures.
normalIntro.cn: penicillin 一个词分两半：霉菌属名与化学后缀，再与它治的病绑在一起记忆。

normal.en: Penicillium is the mould, -in is the substance, so penicillin is the drug made by the mould.
normal.cn: Penicillium 是霉菌，-in 指物质，penicillin 就是这种霉菌造出的药。

normal.en: A course of penicillin is a fixed number of days of treatment that must be finished.
normal.cn: a course of penicillin 是必须吃完的固定疗程。

normal.en: Doctors always ask about penicillin allergy before prescribing it.
normal.cn: 医生开药前总会询问 penicillin allergy（青霉素过敏）。

normal.en: Penicillin resistance grew when the drug was overused.
normal.cn: penicillin resistance 随药物滥用而增长。

normal.en: Compare antibiotic: antibiotic is the general class, penicillin is one famous member of it.
normal.cn: 对比 antibiotic：antibiotic 是总类别，penicillin 是其中著名的成员。

abstract.en: Picture a clean ring in a cloudy dish where the mould sat all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一只雾蒙蒙的培养皿里，霉菌整夜守护出一圈干净的空地。

abstract.en: Think of a family of tablets sharing one surname, with first names added in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一姓药片共享同一个姓，只在前面加上各自的名。

abstract.en: See an old window left open overnight, letting in the spore that changed medicine.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没关的窗，夜里放进了一粒孢子。

examples.en: The doctor prescribed a ten-day course of penicillin.
examples.cn: 医生开了一个十天的青霉素疗程。

examples.en: Penicillin allergy is one of the first things a nurse will ask about.
examples.cn: 护士最先询问的事项之一就是青霉素过敏史。

examples.en: Modern penicillins differ mainly in the side chains attached to the basic molecule.
examples.cn: 现代的各种青霉素主要区别在于连接基础分子上的侧链。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盘尼西林」——听起来像「盘子里长出一片青青林子的毛霉」；这只是谐音联想，真正的来源是霉属青苔般的颜色与笔形孢子。

root: 拉丁语 pencillus（小尾巴）→ 新拉丁语 Penicillium（青霉属，因孢子束呈画笔状得名）→ 英语 penicillin（该霉菌产生的抗菌物质，1929 年弗莱明命名）。

sensesIntro.en: Penicillin starts as the substance itself, then names a whole antibiotic family, the discovery story, and finally the manufactured drug.
sensesIntro.cn: penicillin 先指抗菌物质本身，再指一整类抗生素，也指它的发现故事，最后指工厂生产的药物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear zone of dead bacteria spreading around a spot of green mould.
core.cn: 核心意象：青绿色霉点周围，一圈被清空的死细菌。

branches.en: The substance that clears the dish is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 清空培养皿的那种物质，是这个词的字面义。

branches.en: Tinkering with side chains turns one drug into a family.
branches.cn: 改造侧链，就把一种药变成了一个药物家族。

branches.en: Because the cure and the mould share a name, the discovery is told with the same word.
branches.cn: 因为疗法与霉菌共用一个名字，发现的故事也用这个词来讲。

branches.en: The dish substance and the factory drug are the same molecule at two scales.
branches.cn: 培养皿里的物质与工厂里的药，是同一种分子在不同尺度上的呈现。

branches.en: The story of the first drug is the origin story of the whole family.
branches.cn: 第一种药物的故事，就是整个家族起源的故事。

intro.en: Penicillin is a modern scientific compound: a genus name from Latin plus the -in suffix that marks a substance.
intro.cn: penicillin 是现代科学复合词：拉丁语属名加上标示「物质」的后缀 -in。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word pencillus means a little tail or brush, and it also gives English pencil.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pencillus 意为小尾巴或画笔，英语 pencil 也出自同一个词。

items.meaning: a little tail, a small brush
items.example: The mould was named for the brush-like spores that echoed pencillus.
items.exampleCN: 这种霉菌因孢子束像画笔而得名，正呼应 pencillus。

items.example: Penicillium notatum was the original source of the drug.
items.exampleCN: Penicillium notatum 是最初的药物来源。

items.meaningCN: 标示物质的化学后缀，常用于药物
items.example: The suffix -in turns the genus name into the name of the active substance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -in 把属名变成活性物质的名字。

items.example: Penicillin enters medical English in the nineteen twenties.
items.exampleCN: penicillin 在二十世纪二十年代进入医学英语。

items.example: The plural penicillins covers the whole related group.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式 penicillins 涵盖整个相关族类。

items.example: The enzyme suffix -ase builds penicillinase.
items.exampleCN: 表示酶的词尾 -ase 构成 penicillinase。

items.example: Penicillinase lets bacteria survive the drug.
items.exampleCN: 青霉素酶让细菌能在药物中存活。

items.meaning: a chemical group added to the core
items.meaningCN: 加到核心结构上的化学基团
items.example: Benzyl plus penicillin gives benzylpenicillin.
items.exampleCN: benzyl 加 penicillin 就是 benzylpenicillin。

items.meaning: a penicillin with a changed side chain
items.example: Later drugs such as amoxicillin share the -cillin core.
items.exampleCN: 后来如阿莫西林这样的药共享 -cillin 核心。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 孢子束（用于真菌学描述）

definition_zh: 悔罪的；忏悔的；赎罪的；苦修书
definition_en: showing sorrow for sin and a wish to make amends, or related to penance
core_image: 深夜教堂长椅上，一个人低着头，用掌心轻轻敲自己的胸口
scene: 深夜的教堂里，长椅上只剩下一个人，他低着头，一下一下轻敲自己的胸口。After the pastor finished, the congregation rose and sang a penitential psalm.
sceneCN: 这里 penitential 是「悔罪的、用于忏悔的」（第 1 个义项：表现悔罪并愿赎罪，或与苦修忏悔有关）；句意：牧师讲完后，会众起身唱了一首悔罪诗篇。

derivatives.zh: 由 penitent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「悔罪地」
与 penitential 同根的名词，义为「悔罪；忏悔」
同源名词，义为「苦修；补赎」
由 penitential 同族词干加 -ary 构成，本义「悔罪之所」，现指监狱

senses.title: Showing sorrow for sin
senses.definition: expressing regret for wrong you have done and a wish to make up for it
senses.definitionCN: 对自己所做的错事表示难过，并希望补偿
senses.example: She spoke about her past in a penitential voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一种带着悔意的声音谈起自己的过去。
senses.why: The Latin source paenitentia names sorrow for one s own acts, and the adjective carries that inner turning back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 paenitentia 指对自身行为的懊悔，形容词分词承接了这种内心的回转。

senses.title: Belonging to penance
senses.definition: belonging to the practice of penance, such as fasting, prayer, or bodily hardship
senses.definitionCN: 属于苦修的做法，如禁食、祈祷或身体上的克己
senses.example: Church rules once set out penitential fasting days.
senses.exampleCN: 教会规章曾规定过苦修禁食的日子。
senses.why: Sorrow turned into rule produces a second sense: the outward actions imposed for a sin.
senses.whyCN: 懊悔变成规章之后，就长出第二义：为罪而施加的外在行动。

senses.title: Of the church season
senses.definition: relating to a liturgical season or rite set apart for repentance, especially Lent
senses.definitionCN: 与专门用于悔罪的教会节期或礼仪有关，尤指四旬期
senses.example: The penitential season begins with a quiet, restrained service.
senses.exampleCN: 悔罪期以一场安静克制的礼拜开始。
senses.why: The church fixed whole periods for repentance, so the adjective also marks time rather than persons.
senses.whyCN: 教会为悔罪设定了整段时期，于是这个形容词也用于标注时间而非人。

senses.title: The book of penances
senses.definition: a medieval church handbook listing the penances for particular sins
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪教会手册，逐条列出各种罪应受的补赎
senses.example: No correct penance could be found for the case in any penitential.
senses.exampleCN: 任何悔罪书里都找不到适用于此案的恰当补赎。
senses.why: Medieval writers used the adjective alone as a noun for the book, because penances had to be looked up and set down.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪作者直接用这个形容词作名词指那本书，因为补赎需要查表定额。

intro.en: Penitential comes from Latin paenitentia, repentance, through the Church Latin adjective paenitentialis.
intro.cn: penitential 来自拉丁语 paenitentia（悔罪），经由教会拉丁语形容词 paenitentialis 进入英语。

items.en: A shortened root is reconstructed as pe una, meaning the lack or pain that calls for payment.
items.cn: 学界构拟的形式为 pe una，意为招致偿付的缺乏或痛苦。

items.en: Paenitentia means repentance, linked to paenitet, it causes regret.
items.cn: paenitentia 意为悔罪，与 paenitet（使懊悔）相关。

items.en: Paenitentialis is coined in late antiquity to describe things and seasons of penitence.
items.cn: paenitentialis 在古典后期被造出，用来描述悔罪的事物和节期。

items.en: The French form penitenciel carries the word through the church vocabulary of the north.
items.cn: 法语形式 penitenciel 通过北方的教会词汇把这个词传递下来。

items.en: Penitential enters English as a church word for books and seasons of penance.
items.cn: penitential 以教会用语的身份进入英语，专指悔罪书与悔罪期。

items.en: The word widens to describe any sorrowful, self-punishing manner or mood.
items.cn: 词义扩大，可形容任何懊悔、自责的姿态或情绪。

note.en: Penitential shares its stem with penance, penitent, and the church word for a place of repentance.
note.cn: penitential 与 penance、penitent 以及表示「悔罪之所」的教会词词干相同。

entries.definition: an act you must do to show you are sorry for a sin
entries.definitionCN: 为表示对罪过的悔意而必须做的事

entries.definition: feeling or showing sorrow for wrongdoing
a prison, originally a place of church penance
entries.definitionCN: 监狱，原指教会苦修之所

entries.definition: sorry for something you have done and wanting to change
entries.definitionCN: 对所做的事后悔并想改变的

entries.definition: very sorry and eager to make amends, often in a formal tone
entries.definitionCN: 非常懊悔并急于补救的，语气较正式

entries.definition: the act of making up for a wrong done

normalIntro.en: Penitential sits in the penance family: one stem, several forms, one theme of sorrow and repair.
normalIntro.cn: penitential 属于 penance 词族：同一词干，几种形式，一个主题：懊悔与补救。

normal.en: Penance is the act, penitent is the person feeling it, penitential describes the thing full of it.
normal.cn: penance 是行为，penitent 是悔罪的人，penitential 形容充满悔意的做法或书。

normal.en: A penitential psalm is the church text people pray when they admit a fault.
normal.cn: a penitential psalm 是人们认错时所诵的悔罪诗篇。

normal.en: Penitential fasting is food given up on purpose, not food simply forgotten.
normal.cn: penitential fasting 是有意放弃的食物，而不是忘记吃饭。

normal.en: Doctors spoke of a penitential mood: people apologising for wrongs long past.
normal.cn: penitential mood 指人们为旧错道歉的那种心情。

normal.en: Compare repentant: repentant describes a person feeling sorry, penitential often describes rites, seasons, or books.
normal.cn: 对比 repentant：repentant 描述感到后悔的人，penitential 多描述礼仪、节期或书籍。

abstract.en: Picture one lowered head in a dim nave, and the whole building seems to bow with it.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗教堂里一个人低下头，整座建筑似乎也随他弯下。

abstract.en: Think of Lent as a grey bridge of days you must walk slowly to reach the other side.
abstract.cn: 想象四旬期是一座灰色的日子之桥，只能慢慢走过去。

abstract.en: See a thick book listing one price for every sin, a ledger of regret.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书，为每一种罪标出代价，像一本悔恨的账本。

examples.en: The letter was penitential in tone, full of apologies and promises.
examples.cn: 这封信口气悔罪，满是歉意与承诺。

examples.en: In many traditions, penitential seasons call for simpler meals and more prayer.
examples.cn: 许多传统中的悔罪期要求饮食更简单、祈祷更多。

examples.en: The council drew up a penitential for priests to use when hearing confessions.
examples.cn: 该会议编订了一部供神父听告解时使用的悔罪书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪你疼」——犯错后陪着良心一起疼，那种低头的姿态就是 penitential；这只是谐音联想，真正的来源与拉丁语悔罪词 paenitentia 有关。

root: 拉丁语 paenitentia（悔罪）与动词 paenitet（使懊悔）→ 教会拉丁语 paenitentialis（悔罪的）→ 古法语 penitenciel → 中古英语 penitential，核心义「内心的懊悔」。（更早的印欧词根为学界构拟。）

sensesIntro.en: Penitential moves from the inner sorrow of one person, to the rules of penance, to church seasons, and finally to the book that sets the penances.
sensesIntro.cn: penitential 从一个人的内心懊悔，走到苦修的规则，再到教会的节期，最后指制定补赎的那本书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lowered head and a hand tapping the chest in a quiet church.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静教堂里低下的头与轻敲胸口的手。

branches.en: A person showing regret is the inner, everyday sense.
branches.cn: 表现懊悔的人，是最贴近内心的日常义项。

branches.en: Rules turn regret into actions you must perform.
branches.cn: 规章把懊悔变成必须完成的行为。

branches.en: The calendar sets aside whole weeks for the same regret.
branches.cn: 教会把整周整月划出来，用于同一种懊悔。

branches.en: The book exists because someone has to fix the penances in writing.
branches.cn: 因为补赎必须用文字定下，才会出现这样一本书。

branches.en: Personal sorrow and the shared season describe one feeling at one and many persons.
branches.cn: 一个人的懊悔与众人共度的节期，是同一情感的单数与复数。

intro.en: Penitential is a Latin stem carried by the church, with the -ial adjective ending and a large family of penance words.
intro.cn: penitential 是教会的拉丁语词干加形容词词尾 -ial 构成，周围还有一整族 penance 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin paenitentia means repentance, and paenitet means it causes regret; the stem paenit- runs through all forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 paenitentia 意为悔罪，paenitet 意为使人懊悔，词干 paenit- 贯穿各种形式。

items.example: Paenitentia supplies the whole stem.
items.exampleCN: paenitentia 提供整个词干。

items.example: The verb paenitet names the feeling behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词 paenitet 指向名词背后的那种感受。

items.example: Paenitentialis is the direct model for the English word.
items.exampleCN: paenitentialis 是英语词的直接范本。

items.example: The ending -ial turns a noun stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 把名词词干变成形容词。

items.example: Penitential describes a mood, a psalm, or a season.
items.exampleCN: penitential 可形容情绪、诗篇或节期。

items.example: Penitence names the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: penitence 指这种感受本身。

items.example: Penance is the act a priest may set.
items.exampleCN: penance 是神父可以指定要做的行动。

items.example: Penitent can be a person as well as a mood.
items.exampleCN: penitent 既可指心情，也可指人。

items.example: The adverb suffix -ly gives penitently.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 构成 penitently。

items.example: Penitently describes how someone speaks or kneels.
items.exampleCN: penitently 描述人说话或跪下的方式。

definition_zh: 沉思的；忧伤的；若有所思的
definition_en: thinking deeply and quietly, often about something sad or serious
core_image: 窗边的人托着下巴，目光落在远处，屋里的声音都没进到耳朵里
scene: 雨下了一整下午，窗边的人托着下巴，远处什么也没有看，别人叫他也没听见。She watched the rain by the window, pensive and saying nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 pensive 是「沉思的、若有所思的」（第 1 个义项：安静而专注地想着什么）；句意：她坐在窗边看着雨，若有所思，什么也不说。

pos.zh: 沉思的；忧伤的；若有所思的

derivatives.zh: 由 pensive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「若有所思地」
由 pensive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「若有所思；忧思」
同源词，来自拉丁语 pensio（称量、支付），义为「养老金」
同源词，com- 加 pensare（称量）构成，义为「补偿；弥补」

senses.title: Thinking quietly
senses.definition: thinking in a quiet, absorbed way and partly turned away from the people around you
senses.definitionCN: 安静而专注地想着，多少有点与周围的人隔绝
senses.example: He looked up from the letter with a pensive face.
senses.exampleCN: 他从信上抬起头，一脸沉思。
senses.why: The Latin stem is pensare, to weigh, so a pensive face is a face busy weighing something inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 pensare 意为称量，所以沉思的脸就是在心里称量某事的样子。

senses.title: Quietly sad
senses.definition: quietly sad or heavy with memories, without loud grief
senses.definitionCN: 安静地难过，或带着沉甸甸的回忆，却没有大声的悲伤
senses.example: A pensive pause followed the news.
senses.exampleCN: 消息传来之后，是一阵若有所思的沉默。
senses.why: Weighing turns toward loss: what is pondered most may be what cannot come back, and the mood darkens.
senses.whyCN: 称量会偏向失去：人们反复掂量的往往正是回不来的东西，情绪于是变暗。

senses.title: Of a look or sound
senses.definition: having a calm, thoughtful quality that invites the same mood in others
senses.definitionCN: 具有安静而深思的气质，把同样的心境带给别人
senses.example: The old piano produced a pensive melody.
senses.exampleCN: 那架旧钢琴奏出一段沉静的旋律。
senses.why: Things as well as people can carry the mood, so the adjective spreads from faces to sounds, places, and art.
senses.whyCN: 不只人可以带这种心境，于是这个形容词从脸扩散到声音、场所与艺术。

intro.en: Pensive comes from Old French pensif, from penser, to think, which goes back to Latin pensare, to weigh.
intro.cn: pensive 来自古法语 pensif，源于 penser（思考），更远可追到拉丁语 pensare（称量）。

items.en: Pendere means to hang or weigh, and pensare is its frequentative form.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂或称量，pensare 是它的反复体形式。

items.en: By the late period pensare also carries the sense of thinking about something.
items.cn: 到了古典后期，pensare 也带上「思考某事」的意思。

items.en: Penser means to think, and the adjective pensif means thoughtful.
items.cn: penser 意为思考，形容词 pensif 意为沉思的。

items.en: Pensyf enters English from French as a description of a thoughtful face.
items.cn: pensyf 在十四世纪从法语进入英语，用来描述若有所思的脸。

items.en: The spelling settles as pensive and the sad shade of the word deepens.
items.cn: 拼写稳定为 pensive，词义中忧郁的一层也逐渐加深。

note.en: Pensive sits between thinking and sadness, close to the weigh-word family and to neighbouring moods.
note.cn: pensive 处在「思考」与「忧伤」之间，一端连着「称量」词族，另一端连着邻近的情绪词。

entries.definition: regular money paid after retirement, from a weighing of payments
entries.definitionCN: 退休后定期领取的钱，源自对支付的称量

entries.definition: to make up for something, literally to weigh together
entries.definitionCN: 补偿；弥补，字面意为一起称量

entries.definition: a piece of jewellery that hangs down
entries.definitionCN: 悬挂的饰物，来自 pendere 的「悬挂」义

entries.definition: thinking carefully, or showing care for other people
entries.definitionCN: 深入思考的，或体贴他人的

entries.definition: sad and full of longing for something
thinking dark thoughts for a long time

normalIntro.en: Pensive is a weighing word: the mind on a balance, slowly taking the measure of something.
normalIntro.cn: pensive 是一个称量词：心事放在天平上，慢慢称出分量。

normal.en: Pensive comes from the same weigh family as pension and compensate.
normal.cn: pensive 与 pension、compensate 同属「称量」词族。

normal.en: A pensive mood is quiet, not angry: the sadness is turned inward, not thrown outward.
normal.cn: a pensive mood 是安静的，不是愤怒的：悲伤朝内，不向外发。

normal.en: Pensive people often look away while answering, because part of them is still thinking.
normal.cn: pensive 的人回答时常常望向别处，因为有一部分心思还在想。

normal.en: Pensively is the adverb for how such a person stares or speaks.
normal.cn: 副词 pensively 描述这样一个人凝视或说话的样子。

normal.en: Compare thoughtful: thoughtful also means kind, while pensive never carries that friendly sense.
normal.cn: 对比 thoughtful：thoughtful 还有体贴之意，pensive 从不带这层友好感。

abstract.en: Picture a balance inside the chest, and a small object placed on one side, tick by tick.
abstract.cn: 想象胸腔里有一架天平，小小的事物被放到一端，一格一格地倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a photograph taken in soft evening light, where the face is calm but the eyes are far.
abstract.cn: 想象一张黄昏柔光里的照片，脸很平静，眼睛却望向远处。

abstract.en: Hear one slow piano note left ringing in an empty room after the player has gone.
abstract.cn: 听见演奏者离开后，一个缓慢的琴音仍在空房里回响。

examples.en: She was pensive after reading the letter and did not speak for a long time.
examples.cn: 读完信后她若有所思，很久没说话。

examples.en: The whole class went pensive when the teacher mentioned the old building.
examples.cn: 老师提到那座老建筑时，全班都安静下来，陷入思索。

examples.en: There was a pensive beauty in the empty harbour at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏的空港口有一种沉静的美。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pen 思」——笔尖停在纸上，人正出神地想着，就是 pensive；这只是拆词联想，真正的来源与拉丁语称量词 pensare 有关。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称量）→ 反复体 pensare（称量、考量）→ 古法语 penser（思考）与 pensif（沉思的）→ 中古英语 pensyf → 现代英语 pensive，核心义「在心里称量」。

sensesIntro.en: Pensive begins with quiet thinking, takes on a shade of sadness as the mind weighs what is lost, and then spreads to sounds and places.
sensesIntro.cn: pensive 从安静的思考出发，随着心思称量失去之物而染上忧郁，最后扩散到声音与场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face turned toward the window with a balance working behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：转向窗外的脸，眼睛后面有一架天平在动。

branches.en: Quiet absorption in thought is the first and plainest sense.
branches.cn: 安静地专注于思考，是第一条、最朴素的义项。

branches.en: What is weighed longest tends to be what is lost, so a sad quiet settles in.
branches.cn: 称量最久的往往是失去的东西，于是落下一点安静的悲伤。

branches.en: The mood escapes the face and enters sounds, places, and works of art.
branches.cn: 这种心境离开面容，进入声音、场所与艺术作品。

branches.en: Absorbed thinking and quiet sadness share one stillness of the body.
branches.cn: 沉思与安静的忧郁共享同一副静止的身体姿态。

branches.en: A melody and a sad thought produce the same outward calm in a listener.
branches.cn: 一段旋律与一个悲伤的念头，在听者身上显出同样的平静外表。

intro.en: Pensive is the adjective in the pendere family, where the core idea of hanging becomes weighing and then thinking.
intro.cn: pensive 是 pendere 词族中的形容词，核心义从悬挂变成称量，再变成思考。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere means to hang or weigh, and its frequentative pensare means to weigh carefully and consider.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂或称量，其反复体 pensare 意为仔细称量、考量。

items.example: Pendere gives the family two pictures: something hanging, something being weighed.
items.exampleCN: pendere 给这族词两个画面：悬挂与称量。

items.meaning: to weigh again and again, to consider
items.example: Pensare is the immediate stem of the thinking sense.
items.exampleCN: pensare 是「思考」这一义的直接词干。

items.example: Old French penser carries the meaning north into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 penser 把这层意思带到北方的英语。

items.example: Pensif becomes English pensive after the ending is reshaped.
items.exampleCN: pensif 经词尾改写成为英语 pensive。

items.example: The ending -ive marks a state a person tends to stay in.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 标示人倾向停留的状态。

items.example: Pensive describes a person or a mood.
items.exampleCN: pensive 描述人或一种心境。

items.example: The adverb suffix -ly builds pensively.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 构成 pensively。

items.example: The noun suffix -ness builds pensiveness.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾 -ness 构成 pensiveness。

items.example: Pension keeps the Latin sense of payment weighed out.
items.exampleCN: pension 保留了拉丁语中「称出支付」的含义。

items.example: Compensate joins com- with pensare, to weigh together.
items.exampleCN: compensate 把 com- 与 pensare 组合，意为一起称量。

latinEntries.meaning: a weighed portion of wool or work
latinEntries.meaningCN: 称好的一份羊毛或工作

definition_zh: 五边形；五角形；（P 大写）五角大楼，美国国防部
definition_en: a flat shape with five straight sides; cap. the five-sided building that houses the US Department of Defense
core_image: 纸上一块五条边围成的图形，像一枚切开的五角星外框
scene: 几何课上，老师在黑板上画了一个五边形，让同学数它的五个内角。In the geometry lesson, the teacher drew a pentagon on the board and asked the class to count its five angles.
sceneCN: 这里 pentagon 是「五边形」（第 1 个义项：有五条直边的平面图形）；句意：几何课上，老师在黑板上画了一个五边形，让同学数它的五个内角。

pos.zh: （首字母大写）五角大楼；美国国防部

derivatives.zh: 由 pentagon 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「五边形的」
同用 penta-（五）与 -gram（线条）构成，义为「五角星」
同用 penta- 构成，义为「五项全能运动」

senses.title: A flat shape with five sides
senses.definition: a plane figure bounded by five straight sides and having five angles
senses.definitionCN: 由五条直线段围成、有五个角的平面图形
senses.example: A regular pentagon has five equal sides and five equal angles.
senses.exampleCN: 正五边形的五条边和五个角都相等。
senses.why: The Greek root penta- means five and gonia means angle, so the word names a figure with five angles.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 penta- 意为「五」，gonia 意为「角」，所以这个词直接命名了「有五个角的图形」，先有角的数目，才推得边的数目。

senses.title: The five-sided defense building
senses.definition: the headquarters of the US Department of Defense, a building with five sides
senses.definitionCN: 美国国防部总部，因建筑呈五边形状而得名，常借指美国国防部
senses.example: The Pentagon issued a short statement about the exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 五角大楼就这次演习发布了一份简短声明。
senses.why: The building plan itself is a pentagon, so the shape word became a place name and then a stand-in for the institution.
senses.whyCN: 这座大楼的平面轮廓本身就是一个五边形，于是形状词变成了地名，再借地名指代其中的机构。

senses.title: A five-member group or set
senses.titleCN: 五人（物）组成的团体或组合
senses.definition: a group or set of five people or things, especially in loose or informal use
senses.definitionCN: 由五个人或五样事物组成的一组，多用于非正式或引申说法
senses.example: The founders call their little group a pentagon of talents.
senses.exampleCN: 创始人把这支小团队称作「五人才华组合」。
senses.why: Once the word means five, speakers freely apply it to any set of five, stretching the geometry image into a social one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词的核心被理解为「五」，说话人就会把它套用到任何五人五物的组合上，几何意象由此被借到社会关系里。

senses.title: Pentagon in architecture and symbols
senses.titleCN: 建筑与符号中的五边形母题
senses.definition: a five-sided plan or motif used in buildings, flags, and emblems
senses.definitionCN: 用在建筑平面、旗帜与徽章上的五边形图案
senses.example: The older wing of the museum is built on a pentagon plan.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆较旧的那翼是按五边形平面建造的。
senses.why: Architects borrow the shape name metonymically: the motif keeps the same outline while changing scale from paper to stone.
senses.whyCN: 建筑师直接以形状名称指代设计母题：轮廓不变，只是从纸面放大到石头建筑上，词义因此带上「设计元素」的味道。

senses.title: Figurative pentagon of relationships
senses.definition: an informal figure for a network of five linked parties with shifting alliances
senses.definitionCN: 非正式的比喻说法，指五方相互牵动、格局不断变化的关系网络
senses.example: Critics described the deal as a delicate pentagon of interests.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把这项协议形容为一张微妙的五方利益网。
senses.why: The image of five closed sides suggests tight, self-contained interconnectedness, which suits a closed network of interests.
senses.whyCN: 五条边首尾相接、围成封闭空间的意象，暗示紧密而自足的相互牵连，正好用来形容封闭的利益网络。

intro.en: Pentagon joins Greek penta- (five) with gonia (angle), and the English word has been applied to both the shape and the defense headquarters.
intro.cn: pentagon 由希腊语 penta-（五）与 gonia（角）组合而成，英语里既指图形，也指美国国防部总部。

items.en: Pentagonon combines penta, five, with gonia, angle, literally five-angled.
items.cn: pentagonon 把表「五」的 penta 与表「角」的 gonia 合成「五角」。

items.en: Mathematicians such as the Pythagoreans knew the regular five-sided figure well.
items.cn: 毕达哥拉斯学派等数学家在古风时期已熟悉正五边形。

items.en: Pentagonum passes through Latin as a geometrical term.
items.cn: pentagonum 以几何术语的身份进入拉丁语。

items.en: English pentagon first labels the geometrical figure.
items.cn: 英语 pentagon 最初标注的是几何图形。

items.en: From 1943 the word also names the five-sided US defense building.
items.cn: 自一九四三年起，这个词又指那座五边形的美国国防部大楼。

note.en: Pentagon belongs to the Greek counting family penta- and sits next to other polygon names and shape words.
note.cn: pentagon 属于希腊语「五」的计数词族，与其它多边形名称和形状类词相邻。

entries.definition: having five sides
a five-pointed star figure
entries.definitionCN: 五角星形，与 pentagon 共用 penta-，只是把「角」换成「线」

entries.definition: an athletics contest of five events
entries.definitionCN: 五项全能运动，同用 penta- 构成

entries.definition: Latin for the five-angled figure
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「五角形」，词形与 pentagon 只差词尾

entries.definition: a closed plane figure with many straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 多边形，是 pentagon 所属的上位类

entries.definition: a flat shape with six sides
entries.definitionCN: 六边形，比五边形多一条边

entries.definition: a group of five musicians or performers
entries.definitionCN: 五重奏或五人组合，与引申义「五人组合」义场相近

normalIntro.en: Pentagon is a counting word: penta- gives five and -gon gives angle, so remember the five corners first.
normalIntro.cn: pentagon 是一个计数词：penta- 表五，-gon 表角，先记住五个角，再推五条边。

normal.en: The prefix penta- means five in many borrowings, as in pentathlon.
normal.cn: 前缀 penta- 在诸多借词中表示「五」，如 pentathlon（五项全能）。

normal.en: The suffix -gon means angle, and it also appears in polygon and hexagon.
normal.cn: 后缀 -gon 表示「角」，也出现在 polygon 与 hexagon 里。

normal.en: Add the adjective ending -al to get pentagonal.
normal.cn: 加上形容词后缀 -al 就得到 pentagonal（五边形的）。

normal.en: A regular pentagon is the figure that forms the outline of a five-pointed star.
normal.cn: 正五边形正是五角星轮廓所嵌的那个图形。

normal.en: The US defense headquarters is simply called the Pentagon because of its plan.
normal.cn: 美国国防部总部直接被称为五角大楼，原因就是它的平面图。

abstract.en: Trace five fingers around a table top and close the line.
abstract.cn: 用手掌的五指在桌面上绕一圈，再把线闭合，这就是五边形。

abstract.en: Picture a star outline with the inner corners joined by straight sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗五角星，把五个内角用直线连起来，外框就是五边形。

abstract.en: Hold up one hand and number the fingers from one to five along the edge.
abstract.cn: 举起一只手，沿着手的边缘从一数到五，边走边数就是五条边。

examples.en: Cut the card into a pentagon with five equal sides.
examples.cn: 把卡片剪成一个五边相等的五边形。

examples.en: Pentagons appear on old coins and on sports court markings.
examples.cn: 五边形图案出现在旧硬币上，也出现在球场标线里。

examples.en: Reporters waited near the Pentagon for a briefing.
examples.cn: 记者们在五角大楼附近等待简报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喷他肝」——把「肝」想成一块被切成五边的器官形状，五条边合起来就是五边形；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 penta-（五）+ gonia（角）→ 希腊语 pentagonon（五角形）→ 拉丁语 pentagonum → 英语 pentagon，核心义「五个角的图形」。

sensesIntro.en: Pentagon starts as the name of a five-sided figure, then becomes the name of a real building, and later lends its shape to groups and networks of five.
sensesIntro.cn: pentagon 先指五条边围成的图形，再成为一栋真实建筑的名称，后来又借「五」这一形状去指五人五物的组合与网络。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: five straight sides closing into a single flat ring.
core.cn: 核心意象：五条直边首尾相接，围成一个封闭的平面图形。

branches.en: The plain geometrical figure is the base sense.
branches.cn: 纯粹的几何图形是最基础的义项。

branches.en: A building with five sides turns the shape into a place name.
branches.cn: 五边形大楼把形状变成了地名。

branches.en: Any set of five can be nicknamed a pentagon.
branches.cn: 任何五人五物的组合都可以被戏称为五边形。

branches.en: The same outline moves from paper to stone as an architectural motif.
branches.cn: 同一轮廓从纸面移到石头建筑上，成为设计母题。

branches.en: A closed five-sided network is a vivid figure for tangled relationships.
branches.cn: 封闭的五边网络是形容复杂关系的好比喻。

intro.en: Pentagon is built from the Greek number penta- and the root -gon, and the same pieces appear in many polygon words.
intro.cn: pentagon 由希腊语数词 penta- 与词根 -gon 组成，这些构件也出现在许多多边形名称里。

latinIntro.en: Latin took Greek pentagonon as pentagonum, keeping both the number and the angle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语 pentagonon 接收为 pentagonum，保留了「五」与「角」两部分。

items.example: Penta- counts five.
items.exampleCN: penta- 表示计数上的五。

items.example: The root -gon names angles.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -gon 与「角」有关。

items.example: Greek pentagonon joins the two pieces.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 pentagonon 把两部分拼在一起。

items.example: Latin kept the mathematical meaning.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了数学上的含义。

items.example: The pent- form appears in chemistry names.
items.exampleCN: pent- 这一形式出现在化学名称中。

items.example: Pentagonal adds -al to the noun.
items.exampleCN: pentagonal 是在名词后加 -al。

items.example: Pentagram swaps the angle root for a line root.
items.exampleCN: pentagram 把「角」词根换成了「线」词根。

items.example: Hexagon keeps -gon but changes the number.
items.exampleCN: hexagon 保留 -gon，只改了数字。

items.example: Octagon is another number plus -gon.
items.exampleCN: octagon 同样是数字加 -gon。

definition_en: the family of musical instruments that are struck to make sound; the act of striking something; the tapping of the body to detect signs of disease
core_image: 鼓槌落下，鼓皮猛地一颤，声音从接触点向外荡开
scene: 音乐厅里，鼓手用木槌在定音鼓上敲出滚雷般的声响，整个打击乐声部随之进入。In the concert hall, the drummer struck the timpani with wooden mallets, and a wave of percussion filled the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 percussion 是「打击乐器（声部）」（第 1 个义项：靠敲击发声的乐器及其合奏声部）；句意：音乐厅里，鼓手用木槌在定音鼓上敲出滚雷般的声响，一阵打击乐声随即充满大厅。

derivatives.zh: 由 percussion 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「敲击的；打击乐的」
由 percussion 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，义为「打击乐演奏者」
percussion 的动词形式，义为「叩击；（医）叩诊」

senses.title: The family of struck instruments
senses.definition: musical instruments played by being hit, such as drums, cymbals, and xylophones, and the section of an orchestra that plays them
senses.definitionCN: 靠敲击发声的乐器，如鼓、钹、木琴等，也指管弦乐团中演奏这类乐器的声部
senses.example: Percussion adds rhythm and colour to the orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 打击乐为管弦乐团增添节奏与色彩。
senses.why: The Latin root means to strike hard, and instruments whose sound comes from a blow are named after that act of striking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根意为「重重击打」，凡声音来自一下撞击的乐器，自然就以这个「击打」动作来命名。

senses.title: The act of striking something
senses.definition: the act or effect of hitting something, so that sound or force passes through it
senses.definitionCN: 敲打物体使声音或力量传过去的行为或效果
senses.example: The drilling works by rapid percussion of the rock face.
senses.exampleCN: 这种钻探靠对岩壁的快速冲击来工作。
senses.why: Before it was a music word, it was a general word for any blow, and engineers still use it for tools that hit.
senses.whyCN: 在成为音乐术语之前，它本就是泛指任何击打的一般词，工程领域至今仍用它指靠撞击工作的工具。

senses.title: Tapping the body to listen
senses.definition: the medical technique of tapping the body surface to judge the condition of the parts underneath
senses.definitionCN: 叩击体表、根据回响判断内部器官状况的医学检查方法
senses.example: The doctor used percussion to check the patient for fluid in the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用叩诊检查病人肺里是否有积液。
senses.why: The doctor strikes the chest or abdomen with two fingers, and the sound tapped back reveals what lies under the skin.
senses.whyCN: 医生用两根手指轻敲胸腹，敲回来的声音就是信息，因此同一个「击打」词被借入医学检查。

senses.title: The ignition part of a firearm
senses.definition: the part of a gun or cartridge that is struck to fire
senses.definitionCN: 枪械或弹药中被击打以引发火药燃烧、使枪弹击发的部件
senses.example: The old rifle still uses a percussion cap to fire.
senses.exampleCN: 这把旧步枪仍靠火帽击发。
senses.why: Guns that fire when a small cap is struck were called percussion guns, so the word travelled from music into military hardware.
senses.whyCN: 靠小帽被击打而点火的枪称作击发枪，于是这个词又从音乐一路走到了军械。

senses.title: Sharpness in speech or rhythm
senses.definition: the quality of something spoken or played with sharp, forceful emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 说话或演奏时那种短促、有力、带冲击感的特性
senses.example: Her delivery had the percussion of hammer blows.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话语带着锤击般的力度。
senses.why: The core image of a strike becomes a metaphor: forceful speech also lands like repeated blows.
senses.whyCN: 「一击」的核心意象被搬到言语上：有力的发言听上去就像一记接一记的敲击。

intro.en: Percussion comes from Latin percussio, a striking, from percutere, to strike through, and it moved from hammer blows to drums and to a doctor tapping the body.
intro.cn: percussion 来自拉丁语 percussio（击打），源于 percutere（穿透地打击），词义从锤击转到鼓乐，再到医生叩诊。

items.en: Percutere joins per, through, with quatere, to shake or strike.
items.cn: percutere 由表示「穿透」的 per 与表示「摇动、击打」的 quatere 合成。

items.en: Percussio means a blow or striking hard against something.
items.cn: percussio 意为一次击打、重重撞上某物。

items.en: English first uses percussion for a clash or impact of bodies.
items.cn: 英语最初用 percussion 表示物体相撞或冲击。

items.en: The word spreads to medicine, where doctors percuss the body.
items.cn: 这个词进入医学，指医生叩击身体进行检查。

items.en: Percussion takes on its musical sense, covering drums and other struck instruments.
items.cn: percussion 获得音乐义，涵盖鼓类等靠敲击发声的乐器。

items.en: Modern uses extend to percussion tools, caps, and the percussion section of an orchestra.
items.cn: 现代用法又扩展到冲击式工具、火帽以及乐团的打击乐声部。

note.en: Percussion shares the Latin root for striking with words like percussive and percussionist, and near-meaning words cover drums, rhythm, and impact.
note.cn: percussion 与 percussive、percussionist 共享拉丁语的「击打」词根；近义词则围绕鼓、节奏与冲击展开。

entries.definition: relating to striking or to percussion instruments
a musician who plays percussion instruments
to tap a part of the body for medical examination
entries.definitionCN: （医）叩诊，是 percussion 的动词同源形式

entries.definition: a shaking injury to the brain
entries.definitionCN: 脑震荡，与 percussion 同用拉丁语词根 quatere（摇动），但前缀换成了 con-

entries.definition: a percussion instrument with a skin stretched over a frame
a regular repeated pattern of sound
to hit something forcefully
entries.definitionCN: 打击；敲击，是 percussion 的动词近义概念

normalIntro.en: Percussion is built on the Latin strike root cuss, and the word itself is the act of hitting something, so think of it as the noun of a blow.
normalIntro.cn: percussion 建立在拉丁语「击打」词根 cuss 之上，词本身就是「打一下」这件事的名词，把它记成「一击」。

normal.en: The root -cuss- comes from quatere, to shake, and appears in percussion and concussion.
normal.cn: 词根 -cuss- 源自 quatere（摇动），出现在 percussion 与 concussion 里。

normal.en: The adjective is percussive and the player is a percussionist.
normal.cn: 形容词是 percussive，演奏者叫 percussionist。

normal.en: A percussion instrument is any instrument you hit, such as drums or cymbals.
normal.cn: percussion instrument 就是任何需要敲击的乐器，如鼓或钹。

normal.en: In an orchestra, percussion is a section apart from the strings and the winds.
normal.cn: 在管弦乐团里，percussion 是与弦乐、管乐并列的一个声部。

normal.en: Doctors still percuss the chest in physical examination, a direct legacy of the striking sense.
normal.cn: 医生体检时仍会叩击胸部，这正是「击打」义留在医学里的痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a single mallet falling onto a drumhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一根鼓槌落下，敲在鼓面上。

abstract.en: Feel the short shock that travels up your arm when you hit a table with your knuckles.
abstract.cn: 感受用指节敲桌子时，那股沿着手臂传上来的短促震动。

abstract.en: Imagine the sound wave spreading out from the spot you struck.
abstract.cn: 想象声音从你敲中的那一点向四周荡开。

examples.en: The percussion section began with a soft roll on the cymbals.
examples.cn: 打击乐声部以一声轻柔的镲滚奏开场。

examples.en: The hammer drill uses percussion to break through the concrete.
examples.cn: 电锤靠冲击力穿透混凝土。

examples.en: The physician performed percussion on the patient abdomen.
examples.cn: 医生对病人的腹部做了叩诊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破壳身」——敲破蛋壳那一瞬的「破、壳、声」，正是一击之下声音四散的感觉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿透）+ quatere（摇动、击打）→ percutere（击打）→ 拉丁语 percussio（击打）→ 古法语 percussion → 英语 percussion，核心义为「一击之下贯穿的震动」。

sensesIntro.en: Percussion begins as the act of striking, then names the instruments that are struck, and spreads to a doctor tapping the body, the firing part of a gun, and forceful speech.
sensesIntro.cn: percussion 先指「击打」这一动作，再指被击打的乐器，随后扩散到医生的叩诊、枪械的击发部件以及有力的言语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mallet hitting a drumhead and the sound travelling outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓槌砸在鼓面上，声音向外荡开。

branches.en: Instruments whose sound comes from a blow form the strongest modern sense.
branches.cn: 声音来自一击的乐器构成了最强的现代义项。

branches.en: The general act of hitting is the oldest technical sense.
branches.cn: 泛指敲击与撞击是最古老的术语义项。

branches.en: Medicine borrows the strike as a way to listen through the skin.
branches.cn: 医学把「击打」借来作为隔着皮肤聆听的手段。

branches.en: Both music and firearms fire differently after a small, precise blow.
branches.cn: 音乐与枪械都在一次小而准的击打之后才发生。

branches.en: Forceful speech and tool impacts share the same short, repeated shock.
branches.cn: 有力的言语与工具的冲击共享同一种短促而重复的震感。

intro.en: Percussion is a Latin compound that takes the suffix -ion to name an action, and English builds percussive and percussionist from it.
intro.cn: percussion 是拉丁语复合词，用后缀 -ion 表示动作名词，英语又由它造出 percussive 与 percussionist。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- adds throughness to quatere, to shake, so percussio is a shaking that goes right through.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语前缀 per- 给 quatere（摇动）加上「穿透」意味，所以 percussio 是一次贯穿的震击。

items.example: The prefix per- gives a sense of going through.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 带来「穿透」意味。

items.example: Quatere is the shaking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: quatere 是这一词族「摇动」的根。

items.example: Percutere combines strike with throughness.
items.exampleCN: percutere 把击打与穿透合在一起。

items.example: The root -cuss- shows in percussion.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -cuss- 体现在 percussion 中。

items.meaning: act or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或其结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion turns striking into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把「击打」变成名词。

items.example: Percussio is the direct source form.
items.exampleCN: percussio 是直接来源形式。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms percussive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 percussive。

items.meaningCN: 表示从事某活动之人的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ist forms percussionist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 percussionist。

items.example: Concussion shares the shaking root.
items.exampleCN: concussion 共享「摇动」这一词根。

items.example: Percuss is the short verb form.
items.exampleCN: percuss 是简短的动词形式。

definition_zh: 多年生植物；终年不断的；长期的；反复出现的
definition_en: a plant that lives for more than two years; continuing or lasting through the whole year and from year to year
core_image: 院子角落那丛花，叶子枯了又发，年年从原来的根里重新长出来
scene: 院子里的那丛紫锥花每年开春都会从旧根处重新冒芽。In the garden, the clump of coneflowers puts up fresh shoots from its old roots every spring, confirming it as a true perennial.
sceneCN: 这里 perennial 是「多年生植物」（第 1 个义项：能连续多年存活的植物）；句意：院子里的那丛紫锥花每年开春都会从旧根处重新冒芽，正是典型的多年生植物。

pos.zh: 长久的；长期存在的；反复出现的

derivatives.zh: 由 perennial 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「常年地；一直地」
由 perennial 加 -ity 构成的抽象名词，义为「多年存续；长期性」
由 perennial 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使成为多年生；使长期化」

senses.title: A plant that lives for years
senses.definition: a plant that lives for more than two growing seasons and comes back each year
senses.definitionCN: 成活超过两个生长季、每年都会重新发芽的植物
senses.example: This border is planted with perennials that flower every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这片花坛种的是每年夏天开花的多年生植物。
senses.why: Latin per, through, and annus, year, meet in perennis, lasting through the years, and plants that outlive a single season are named after that span.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per（贯穿）与 annus（年）合成 perennis（贯穿多年），能活过一个又一个年头的植物自然就用这个词来命名。

senses.title: Continuing all year round
senses.definition: that continues, flows, or is present throughout the whole year without a break
senses.definitionCN: 全年持续、流淌或存在而不断绝的
senses.example: The village sits beside a perennial stream that never dries up.
senses.exampleCN: 村子旁边有一条终年不断的溪流，从没有干涸过。
senses.why: Perennis meant lasting the whole year, so a river, stream, or spring that does not dry up is described as perennial.
senses.whyCN: perennis 本义是「贯穿整年」，所以一条不会断流的河、溪或泉就被称作「终年不断的」。

senses.title: A problem that keeps returning
senses.definition: a difficulty or complaint that recurs year after year and is never fully settled
senses.definitionCN: 年复一年反复出现、始终无法彻底解决的困难或抱怨
senses.example: Traffic jams are a perennial problem in this city.
senses.exampleCN: 堵车是这座城市的长期问题。
senses.why: If a thing keeps coming back every year, speakers extend the yearly image to any endlessly repeated difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 只要某种麻烦年年都会回来，说话人就把「逐年」的意象延伸到任何反复出现的难题上。

senses.title: Enduring and long-lasting
senses.definition: lasting or valued for a very long time rather than just briefly
senses.definitionCN: 长期存在或长期被看重，而非仅短暂一时的
senses.example: Her books have become a perennial favourite with young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书已成为年轻读者经久不衰的心头好。
senses.why: The sense of lasting through years shifts from calendar time to durability of reputation or taste.
senses.whyCN: 「经年不衰」的意思从自然时间转到名声与品味上，于是发生了「持久」。

senses.title: A recurring pattern
senses.definition: appearing or happening again at regular intervals in a way that seems endless
senses.definitionCN: 以固定间隔一再出现、仿佛没完没了的
senses.example: The region faces perennial water shortages every dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区每到旱季都会面临水资源短缺。
senses.why: The plant that comes back each spring gives a natural image of periodic return, which is then applied to seasons and cycles.
senses.whyCN: 植物每年春天重新发芽，天然就是「周期性回归」的画面，这一画面随后被套用到季节与循环上。

intro.en: Perennial comes from Latin perennis and per, through, plus annus, year, meaning lasting through the year or years.
intro.cn: perennial 来自拉丁语 perennis，即 per（贯穿）与 annus（年）的组合，意为「贯穿整年或多年」。

items.en: Annus means year and anchors the whole family, as in annual and anniversary.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，是整个词族的结构基础，annual、anniversary 都由此而来。

items.en: Perennis joins per, through, with annus, year, meaning lasting through the years.
items.cn: perennis 把 per（贯穿）与 annus（年）合起来，意为贯穿多年。

items.en: The Romans applied perennis to springs that never dried up.
items.cn: 罗马人用 perennis 来形容不会枯竭的泉水。

items.en: English perennial first describes plants and streams that last all year.
items.cn: 英语 perennial 最初形容全年不枯的植物与溪流。

items.en: The word broadens to perennial problems, perennial favourites, and periodic patterns.
items.cn: 词义进一步扩展到长期问题、经久不衰的宠儿以及周期性现象。

note.en: Perennial belongs to the Latin yearly family of annual, biennial, and perennially, and sits near meaning words such as perpetual and lasting.
note.cn: perennial 属于拉丁语「年」的词族，与 annual、biennial、perennially 同源；近义词包括 perpetual、lasting 等。

entries.definition: continually, year after year
happening once a year or lasting one year
entries.definitionCN: 每年的；一年生的，与 perennial 共用 annus（年）

entries.definition: happening every two years or living two years
entries.definitionCN: 两年一次的；两年生的，处在 annual 与 perennial 中间

entries.definition: allowing liquid to pass through
entries.definitionCN: 可渗透的；只是拼写以 per- 开头且形近，词源与 perennial 不同

entries.definition: continuing forever or for a very long time without stopping
entries.definitionCN: 永久的；无休止的，比 perennial 语气更强调「不停」

entries.definition: lasting forever
entries.definitionCN: 永恒的；持久的，多用于文学性表达

entries.definition: happening again and again
entries.definitionCN: 反复发生的，对应 perennial 表示周期性出现的用法

normalIntro.en: Perennial is yearly arithmetic: per- means through and -ennial comes from annus, year, so the word means going through the years.
normalIntro.cn: perennial 的拆法像算年纪：per- 表贯穿，-ennial 来自 annus（年），合起来就是「贯穿多年」。

normal.en: The root annus, year, is shared by annual, biennial, and anniversary.
normal.cn: 词根 annus（年）共享于 annual、biennial、anniversary。

normal.en: The prefix per- means through, as in permafrost keeping ice through all seasons.
normal.cn: 前缀 per- 表「贯穿」，如 permafrost（永久冻土）指冰贯穿四季。

normal.en: Perennial plants are set against annuals, which sprout, seed, and die in one year.
normal.cn: 多年生植物与一年生植物相对，后者一年内就发芽、结籽、枯死。

normal.en: Add -ly to get perennially, as in a perennially popular dish.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得到 perennially，如「一直受欢迎的菜」。

normal.en: A perennial problem is one that comes back each season, like weeds in the same bed.
normal.cn: perennial problem 指每季都会回来、像同一花坛里长不完的杂草那样的问题。

abstract.en: See a flower bed where the stems die but the roots wait underground.
abstract.cn: 想象一片花坛：茎叶枯了，根却一直藏在地下等待。

abstract.en: Watch a stream run through all four seasons without stopping.
abstract.cn: 看着一条溪流穿过四季，一直在流。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with the same page torn open again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，同一张纸被一次次翻回来。

examples.en: Gardeners value perennials because they need less replanting each spring.
examples.cn: 园丁重视多年生植物，因为每年春天不必重新栽种。

examples.en: Fewer young people are willing to take on that perennial hard job.
examples.cn: 愿意接手那份常年辛苦工作的人越来越少了。

examples.en: His sense of humour has proved perennially popular on stage.
examples.cn: 他的幽默感在舞台上一直广受欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「配年两」——把它配给「一年又一年」：每年都发芽、都还在，就是多年生；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（贯穿）+ annus（年）→ perennis（贯穿整年的）→ 拉丁语 perenniale / 近代英语 perennial，核心义「贯穿年复一年」。

sensesIntro.en: Perennial starts from the idea of lasting through the years: first a plant that comes back every season, then a stream running all year, then anything that keeps returning or enduring.
sensesIntro.cn: perennial 从「贯穿多年」出发：先指每年都重新长出的植物，再指终年不断的水流，最后指任何反复出现或长久存在的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same root sending up new shoots year after year.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个根，年复一年地抽出新芽。

branches.en: The plant that outlives a single season is the concrete base sense.
branches.cn: 活过一季的植物是具体的基础义项。

branches.en: A stream that never dries keeps the calendar meaning.
branches.cn: 终年不干的溪流保留了「整年」的本义。

branches.en: A yearly trouble turns into the perennial problem sense.
branches.cn: 年年出现的麻烦转化为「长期问题」。

branches.en: Problems that return and patterns that recur share the same endless repetition.
branches.cn: 老问题与反复出现的规律共享同一种「没完没了」的重复感。

branches.en: What lives long in the garden becomes what is loved long in taste or reputation.
branches.cn: 园子里活得久的，变成了品味与名声里被爱得久的。

intro.en: Perennial joins the prefix per- with the yearly root ann-, and English builds perennially and perenniality around it.
intro.cn: perennial 把前缀 per- 与表「年」的词根 ann- 结合起来，英语再围绕它造出 perennially 与 perenniality。

latinIntro.en: Latin per, through, plus annus, year, become perennis, meaning lasting through the years.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 per（贯穿）加 annus（年）成为 perennis，意为贯穿多年、经年不衰。

items.example: The prefix per- gives a through sense.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 带来「贯穿」的意义。

items.example: The root ann- also gives annual.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ann- 也构成 annual。

items.example: Annus is the measure the word builds on.
items.exampleCN: annus 是这个词所依托的度量单位。

items.example: Perennis names water that never dries.
items.exampleCN: perennis 指永不干涸的水。

items.example: The suffix -al gives the modern adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成现代形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms perennially.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 perennially。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的抽象名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms perenniality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 perenniality。

items.example: Annual shares the yearly root.
items.exampleCN: annual 共享「年」词根。

items.example: Biennial adds a two to the year root.
items.exampleCN: biennial 在「年」词根上加了「二」。

items.meaning: to survive from one season to the next
items.example: Perennate describes plants that live on through winter.
items.exampleCN: perennate 描述能越过冬天继续存活的植物。

definition_zh: 穿孔；打孔；刺穿；在纸上打出齿孔线
definition_en: to make a hole or a line of small holes through something
core_image: 一枚钢针把纸面戳穿，对着光能看见一个小孔
scene: 售票窗口前，职员把一叠车票放进机器，针头一起落下，整张纸被扎出一排小孔。At the ticket window, the clerk ran the sheets through a machine and perforated them with a neat line of holes.
sceneCN: 这里 perforate 是「穿孔、打孔」（第 1 个义项：在物上扎出孔洞）；句意：售票窗口前，职员把一叠车票放进机器，针头一起落下，整张纸被扎出一排小孔。

collocations.zh: 穿孔很深的；布满孔洞的

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ion 构成名词，义为「穿孔；孔洞」
过去分词作形容词，义为「打过孔的；有孔的」
加后缀 -or 构成名词，义为「打孔机；打孔者」

senses.title: To make holes through something
senses.definition: to make a hole or a row of holes through paper, metal, or other material
senses.definitionCN: 在纸、金属等材料上扎出孔洞或一排小孔
senses.example: The clerk perforated the tickets along a dotted line.
senses.exampleCN: 职员沿虚线把车票打出一排孔。
senses.why: The Latin prefix per- means through, so the verb is simply the act of driving a hole clear through a surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 per- 意为「穿过」，所以这个词就是让孔洞贯穿一个平面的动作。

senses.title: To pierce a body part
senses.definition: to make a hole in a part of the body, especially the eardrum or the gut, usually by injury or disease
senses.definitionCN: 因受伤或患病而在身体部位（尤指鼓膜或肠壁）上形成穿孔
senses.example: The infection can perforate the lining of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 这种感染可能使胃壁穿孔。
senses.why: The same through image applies to the body: something makes a breach that goes from one side of a tissue to the other.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「贯穿」意象也用于身体：某物把组织从一侧穿透到另一侧。

senses.title: To put a line of small holes in paper
senses.definition: to punch small holes at regular intervals so that paper can be torn along that line
senses.definitionCN: 按固定间隔打出小孔，使纸能沿这条线撕开
senses.example: The stamps are perforated so they can be separated.
senses.exampleCN: 邮票打过齿孔，便于一张张撕开。
senses.why: A row of holes is only holes with a purpose: the perforations decide where the sheet will give way.
senses.whyCN: 一排小孔不只是孔：齿孔决定了整张纸会从哪里断开。

senses.title: To break through a defensive line
senses.definition: to break through an enemy line or barrier and open a way into it
senses.definitionCN: 突破敌军阵线或屏障，在其中打开缺口
senses.example: The attackers perforated the line with armoured vehicles.
senses.exampleCN: 进攻方用装甲车撕开了防线。
senses.why: A defence is a surface, and to break it is to make the one hole that lets force pass straight through.
senses.whyCN: 防御是一道面，突破就是在它上面开出能让力量直穿过去的孔。

intro.en: Perforate comes from Latin perforare, built on per- meaning through and forare meaning to bore or pierce. English took it in the sixteenth century for the act of boring through a solid.
intro.cn: perforate 来自拉丁语 perforare，由 per-（穿过）与 forare（钻孔、刺穿）构成。英语在十六世纪借入，指把实体钻穿的动作。

items.en: Per- is a Latin preposition and prefix meaning through or across.
items.cn: per- 是拉丁语介词兼前缀，意为「穿过、贯穿」。

items.en: Forare means to bore or pierce; the related noun foramen, an opening, survives in anatomy.
items.cn: forare 意为钻孔、刺穿；相关名词 foramen（孔、开口）保留在解剖学术语里。

items.en: The compound verb means to bore through, used of cloth, wood, and metal.
items.cn: 复合动词 perforare 意为钻穿，用于布、木、金属等物。

items.en: The past participle perforat, marked with holes, appears in English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语出现过去分词 perforat，意为「打过孔的」。

items.en: In the nineteenth century perforate is fixed to the punched lines of stamps and tickets, and medicine later adds the sense of a pierced organ.
items.cn: 十九世纪，perforate 固定用来指邮票与车票上的齿孔线；医学随后又添了器官穿孔一义。

note.en: Perforate belongs to the Latin family of boring and piercing, and it is close to the everyday words for punching and for holes.
note.cn: perforate 属于拉丁语表示「钻孔、刺穿」的词族，与日常表示打孔和孔洞的词关系很近。

entries.definition: a hole made through something
having no holes, especially an uncut stamp
entries.definitionCN: 无孔的；未打齿孔的（尤指邮票）

entries.definition: an opening through a bone
entries.definitionCN: 骨上的孔（同出拉丁语 forare）

entries.definition: to go into or through something with a sharp point
to make a hole with a tool or machine
to make a hole with a rotating tool

normalIntro.en: Perforate is built from a prefix meaning through and a stem meaning to bore.
normalIntro.cn: perforate 由意为「穿过」的前缀和意为「钻孔」的词干构成。

normal.en: Per- means through, so perforate is to bore a way through.
normal.cn: per- 意为穿过，perforate 就是钻穿一层东西。

normal.en: The noun perforation keeps the same work and adds -ion.
normal.cn: 名词 perforation 保留同样的含义，只多了 -ion。

normal.en: Perforated metal is used for screens because air passes through the holes.
normal.cn: perforated metal 常做筛网，因为空气能穿过那些孔。

normal.en: A perforated stamp has a line of tiny holes waiting to be torn.
normal.cn: 打齿孔的邮票有一排小孔，等着被撕开。

normal.en: Compare pierce: pierce needs a sharp point, perforate only needs a hole through.
normal.cn: 对比 pierce：pierce 要靠尖头，perforate 只强调孔把东西穿通了。

abstract.en: Picture a needle going in on one side and coming out the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针从一边进去，从另一边出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a long strip of tickets that splits along its dots.
abstract.cn: 想象一整条票沿着一排小孔裂开。

abstract.en: Think of a paper target where the arrow point has gone right through.
abstract.cn: 想象纸靶被箭头整个穿过去。

examples.en: Workers perforate the metal sheet before it is bent into a screen.
examples.cn: 工人先把金属板打孔，再把它弯成筛网。

examples.en: The perforated pages can be torn out and filed.
examples.cn: 打过孔的页面可以撕下来归档。

examples.en: Doctors warned that the ulcer might perforate the gut wall.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，溃疡可能使肠壁穿孔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迫（per）斧（fo）瑞（re）特（te）」——像被斧头逼着捅穿一块板子；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿过）+ forare（钻孔、刺穿）→ 拉丁语 perforare（钻穿）→ 英语 perforate，核心义「让孔洞贯穿一个面」。

sensesIntro.en: Perforate starts with the plain act of boring through a material, then narrows to a pierced organ and a punched line, and widens to breaking through a line of defence.
sensesIntro.cn: perforate 先指在材料上钻出孔洞这个基本动作，再收窄为器官穿孔与打齿孔线，最后扩展为突破防线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steel needle passing clean through a sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根钢针把纸面整个穿通。

branches.en: Making holes through a material is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 在材料上穿孔是最基本的义项。

branches.en: A pierced body part is the medical branch of the same image.
branches.cn: 身体部位穿孔是同一意象的医学分支。

branches.en: A punched line is holes put to a purpose.
branches.cn: 打齿孔线是为了让纸撕开而打的一排孔。

branches.en: Both a sheet of metal and a defence can be given a hole to pass through.
branches.cn: 金属板与防线都可以被开出一个可以穿过的缺口。

branches.en: A torn stamp and a torn organ both follow a line of holes that has already weakened the surface.
branches.cn: 撕开的邮票与穿孔的器官沿的是同一逻辑：孔线已经把表面弄薄弱了。

intro.en: Perforate wraps a Latin prefix of going through around a Latin verb of boring, and English builds the words for holes and machines on that stem.
intro.cn: perforate 在拉丁语「钻孔」动词外围加了表示「穿过」的前缀，英语在这个词干上造出了表示孔洞和机器的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- means through, and forare means to bore; perforare joins them into one verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 per- 意为穿过，forare 意为钻孔，perforare 把两者合成一个动词。

items.example: Per- puts the idea of going through into the verb.
items.exampleCN: per- 把「穿过去」的意思加进动词。

items.example: Forare is the core verb of boring.
items.exampleCN: forare 是表示钻孔的核心动词。

items.example: Perforare is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: perforare 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Foramen still names openings in bone.
items.exampleCN: foramen 至今指骨上的孔。

items.example: The suffix -ion builds perforation from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 由动词造出 perforation。

items.meaning: a hole, or the act of making one
items.example: Perforation names both the hole and the act.
items.exampleCN: perforation 既指孔，也指穿孔这一动作。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms the adjective perforated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成形容词 perforated。

items.example: Perforated paper tears along its line.
items.exampleCN: 打孔纸会沿着孔线撕开。

items.example: A perforator cuts holes at a fixed spacing.
items.exampleCN: 打孔机按固定间距打孔。

definition_zh: 周长；周边；边界线；外围（地带）
definition_en: the outer edge of a closed shape or an area, and the length of that edge
core_image: 一支铅笔沿着操场边线绕行一周，画出一条首尾相接的细线
scene: 测绘员把卷尺绕过长方形花园的四条边，逐段报出长度，最后加总出一个数。The surveyor walked the rope right round the rectangular garden to measure its perimeter.
sceneCN: 这里 perimeter 是「周长」（第 1 个义项：封闭图形边界线的总长度）；句意：测绘员把卷尺绕过长方形花园的四条边，逐段报出长度，最后加总出一个数。

derivatives.zh: 由 perimeter 加 -ic 构成，义为「周边的；周界的」
加后缀 -y 构成，义为「视野测量（眼科）」
由形容词 perimetric 再加 -ally 构成，义为「按周边地」

senses.title: The length of the outer edge
senses.definition: the total length of the line that marks the border of a closed shape or area
senses.definitionCN: 封闭图形或区域的边界线的总长度
senses.example: A square with sides of two metres has a perimeter of eight metres.
senses.exampleCN: 边长两米的正方形，周长是八米。
senses.why: Greek metro means measure, so a perimeter is literally the measuring line that runs all the way round a shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 metro 意为「测量」，所以 perimeter 字面就是绕图形一周的那条测量线。

senses.title: The border itself
senses.definition: the boundary line of a shape or area, seen as a line rather than as a length
senses.definitionCN: 图形或区域的边界线本身，强调的是线而不是长度
senses.example: She traced the perimeter of the island on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 她在地图上描出这座岛的边线。
senses.why: The same word can name the line and the length, because the act of walking round measures one by drawing the other.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指线也指长度，因为绕行测量的过程就是把线画出来的过程。

senses.title: The edge of a guarded place
senses.definition: the outer edge of a place that is watched or protected, especially an airfield or a camp
senses.definitionCN: 受守卫或保护的场所的外缘，尤指机场或营地的周边
senses.example: Guards patrolled the perimeter of the airfield all night.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵整夜在机场外围巡逻。
senses.why: A guarded site is treated like a closed figure, and its perimeter is the line where watching begins.
senses.whyCN: 受守卫的场所被当作一个封闭图形，而它的周界正是守卫开始的那条线。

senses.title: The range of vision
senses.definition: the outer limit of what can be seen or felt when looking straight ahead
senses.definitionCN: 直视前方时能看到或感觉到的最外缘
senses.example: The car appeared at the perimeter of his vision.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆车出现在他视野的边缘。
senses.why: Sight has a border too, and the edge of the visible field keeps the shape of a ring around the centre.
senses.whyCN: 视觉也有边界，可见范围的外缘围绕中央形成一个环。

intro.en: Perimeter joins Greek peri- meaning around to metron meaning measure. Classical Greek perimetron was an adjective used by geometers for the line around a figure, and English took the noun in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: perimeter 由希腊语 peri-（绕、周围）与 metron（测量）组成。古典希腊语的 perimetron 是几何学家用来指「环绕图形之线」的形容词，英语在十六世纪借入其名词形式。

items.en: Peri- is a Greek preposition meaning around or round about.
items.cn: peri- 是希腊语介词，意为「绕、在周围」。

items.en: Metron means measure, and gives English metre, metric, and geometry.
items.cn: metron 意为测量，是英语 metre、metric 与 geometry 的来源。

items.en: Geometers use perimetron for the line drawn round a figure, so the word enters mathematics from the start.
items.cn: 几何学家用 perimetron 指环绕图形画出的线，这个词一开始就属于数学。

items.en: Latin keeps the Greek shape in perimetros, a term of geometry and later of astronomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 perimetros 保留希腊语的形式，用于几何，后来也用于天文。

items.en: English borrows perimeter with its geometrical sense. The sense of a guarded edge is much later and comes through the army.
items.cn: 英语借入 perimeter 时用的是几何义。受守卫的边沿一义出现得晚得多，经由军界传开。

note.en: Perimeter is framed by the Latin and Greek words for measuring a shape, and by the everyday words for the line around it.
note.cn: perimeter 处于拉丁语与希腊语「测量图形」用词的框架之中，也与日常表示「环绕之线」的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to a perimeter
relating to measurement
entries.definitionCN: 测量的；公制的（同出希腊语 metron）

entries.definition: a measurable factor that defines a system
entries.definitionCN: 界定系统的可测因素；只是长得像，词源不同

entries.definition: the line or distance around a circle
a line that marks the limit of an area
the outer shape or edge of something

normalIntro.en: Perimeter is a Greek measure-word wrapped in a prefix that means around.
normalIntro.cn: perimeter 是一个希腊语测量词，外面套着意为「环绕」的前缀。

normal.en: Peri- means around, and metron means measure, so the word is a measure around.
normal.cn: peri- 意为环绕，metron 意为测量，合起来就是「绕一圈来量」。

normal.en: The plural is the easy one: add -s to get perimeters.
normal.cn: 复数很好记：直接加 -s 成为 perimeters。

normal.en: A perimeter fence is the line where the guarding starts.
normal.cn: perimeter fence 就是守卫开始的那条围栏线。

normal.en: Circum- and peri- both mean around, but circumference belongs to circles only.
normal.cn: circum- 与 peri- 都表示环绕，但 circumference 只用于圆。

normal.en: A parameter is a measured value; only spelling, not history, links it to this word.
normal.cn: parameter 是被测量的数值；它与本词的关联只在拼写上，不在词源上。

abstract.en: Picture an ant walking one full round along the rim of a coin and back to its start.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚂蚁沿硬币边沿走满整整一圈，回到起点。

abstract.en: Think of a lawn cut as a thin line, then pulled straight and laid beside a ruler.
abstract.cn: 把一圈草坪想成一根细线，再把它拉直放到尺子旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine the fence line of a camp lit up at night for the whole visible ring.
abstract.cn: 想象营地四周的围栏整圈在夜里亮起灯来。

examples.en: You need the perimeter to work out how much fencing the field requires.
examples.cn: 要先求周长，才能算出场院需要多少围栏。

examples.en: The children walk the perimeter of the yard before the signal is given.
examples.cn: 信号发出之前，孩子们围着院子的边线走。

examples.en: Cameras cover the perimeter of the building day and night.
examples.cn: 摄像头日夜监控这座建筑的外围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮（pe）瑞（ri）米（mi）特（ter）」——想象给一块地的外皮量周长的软尺；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 peri-（环绕）+ metron（测量）→ 希腊语几何词 perimetron（绕行量出之线）→ 拉丁语 perimetros → 英语 perimeter，核心义「绕图形一周量出的界线」。

sensesIntro.en: Perimeter begins in the geometer class with the measured line around a figure, then splits into the line and the length, and later stretches to guarded ground and to the edge of sight.
sensesIntro.cn: perimeter 起于几何学，指绕图形量出的那条线；随后既指线也指长度，再延伸到受守卫的地带与视野边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil tracing one full loop around a field.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅笔绕着场地描出完整的一圈。

branches.en: The measured length is the arithmetic sense.
branches.cn: 量出的长度是算术义项。

branches.en: The border line is the same word naming the drawing rather than the figure.
branches.cn: 边界线义指称的是那条线本身，而不是数字。

branches.en: A guarded site has a perimeter where watching begins.
branches.cn: 受守卫的场所以周界作为警戒起点。

branches.en: A camp and a palace share one closed edge, one named by the surveyor and one by the guard.
branches.cn: 营地与宫殿共用一条闭合的边，只是测绘员与卫兵各给了它一个名字。

branches.en: A shape is measured around its rim, and sight in the same way runs out to a rim.
branches.cn: 图形绕边量出长度，视线同样一直延伸到某个边缘。

intro.en: Perimeter is a Greek compound carried through Latin: the prefix peri- goes with metron, the measure. English keeps the same pieces in other words for measuring.
intro.cn: perimeter 是通过拉丁语传来的希腊语复合词：前缀 peri- 与表示测量的 metron 搭配。英语在其他表示测量的词里保留了同样的构件。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are Greek peri- around and metron measure; Latin adopted the same shape as perimetros.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是希腊语 peri-（环绕）与 metron（测量）；拉丁语以 perimetros 的形式接收了它。

items.example: Peri- tells you the line goes all the way round.
items.exampleCN: peri- 告诉你这条线是绕着走的。

items.example: Metron supplies the measure inside the word.
items.exampleCN: metron 提供词里的「测量」义。

items.meaning: measured around, running round a figure
items.meaningCN: 绕行量出的；环绕图形的
items.example: Geometers used perimetron for the ring of a figure.
items.exampleCN: 几何学家用 perimetron 指图形的环线。

items.example: Perimetros carried the term into Latin.
items.exampleCN: perimetros 把这一术语带进拉丁语。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms perimetric.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 perimetric。

items.example: Perimetric refers to what lies on the edge.
items.exampleCN: perimetric 指位于边界上的。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或领域的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y builds perimetry in medicine.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 在医学中构成 perimetry。

items.meaning: the line around a shape, or its length
items.example: Perimeter keeps both the line and the length.
items.exampleCN: perimeter 既指线，也指长度。

items.example: Latin circum- works like Greek peri- in circumference.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 circum- 在 circumference 里与希腊语 peri- 作用相同。

definition_zh: 期刊；定期出版物；周期性的
definition_en: a magazine or journal that appears at regular intervals, or something that happens at such intervals
core_image: 阅览架上排着一叠同款杂志，每期封面日期挨着往后翻
scene: 图书馆的阅览架上，同一本学术杂志从春季号排到冬季号，每期封面都是同一个刊名。The library shelves every issue of the periodical from spring to winter.
sceneCN: 这里 periodical 是「期刊」（第 1 个义项：按固定间隔连续出版的杂志或刊物）；句意：图书馆的阅览架上，同一本学术杂志从春季号排到冬季号，每期封面都是同一个刊名。

derivatives.zh: 由 periodical 加 -ly 构成，义为「定期地；周期性地」
由 periodic 加 -ity 构成，义为「周期性」
基础名词，义为「时期；周期」

senses.title: A journal issued at fixed intervals
senses.definition: a magazine or journal on a particular subject that is published at regular intervals, such as weekly or monthly
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某一主题、按周或按月等固定间隔连续出版的杂志或学术刊物
senses.example: The archive holds every periodical printed in the city since 1900.
senses.exampleCN: 这家档案馆保存着该市自 1900 年以来印刷的全部期刊。
senses.why: The Latin affix -al turns a cycle of time into a thing that comes round again, so the noun names a publication that returns like a clock.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词尾 -al 把「时间循环」变成「一次次重现之物」，所以这个名词指的是一本像钟表一样按时回来的刊物。

senses.title: Happening at regular intervals
senses.definition: happening again after a regular interval rather than once for all
senses.definitionCN: 按固定间隔反复发生，而不是只发生一次
senses.example: The auditors make periodical visits to the factory floor.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员会定期到生产车间察看。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the original geometric picture of going round and coming back, applied to events instead of lines.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了最原始的几何画面：绕一圈又回来，只是把对象换成了事件。

senses.title: Writing that appears in such a journal
senses.definition: the kind of writing or publication carried by journals rather than by books
senses.definitionCN: 由期刊而非图书刊载的文章或出版形式
senses.example: Historians now read periodicals as closely as they read books.
senses.exampleCN: 如今历史学家读期刊的用心程度不亚于读图书。
senses.why: When a whole class of publications gets a name, that name often comes to stand for the medium itself, not for one issue.
senses.whyCN: 当一整类出版物有了名字，这个名字往往转而代表这种媒介本身，而不是某一期。

senses.title: A round-trip route
senses.definition: a journey that goes the long way round and returns to its starting point, now mostly dated
senses.definitionCN: 绕远一圈又回到起点的行程，现多为旧义
senses.example: The old maps still show the periodical route of the coach.
senses.exampleCN: 旧地图上仍标着马车绕行的环线。
senses.why: The earliest meaning of the root was literally a going around a circuit, and a route that comes back is that circuit on a map.
senses.whyCN: 词根的早期含义字面上就是「绕行一圈」，而一条归于起点的路线正是地图上画的那一圈。

intro.en: Periodical goes back to Greek periodos, a going around, formed from peri- around and hodos, way. Latin periodus and the English adjective periodic lead to the noun and adjective periodical, which English records in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: periodical 可追溯到希腊语 periodos（绕行一圈），由 peri-（环绕）与 hodos（路）构成。经拉丁语 periodus 与英语形容词 periodic，再到名词兼形容词 periodical，英语在十七世纪见到这个词。

items.en: Hodos means way or road, and also appears in method and period.
items.cn: hodos 意为路、道路，也见于 method 与 period。

items.en: Periodos is a going round, a circuit, applied to orbits and to rounded phrases.
items.cn: periodos 意为绕行、一圈，用于天体轨道，也用于首尾收口的句子。

items.en: Latin periodus keeps the astronomical and rhetorical senses of the Greek word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 periodus 保留了希腊词的星象义与修辞义。

items.en: English forms periodic and then periodical, first as adjectives meaning recurring, then as a noun for a publication that keeps coming round.
items.cn: 英语先有 periodic，后有 periodical，起初是意为「反复出现的」形容词，随后成为指代按期出版的刊物的名词。

items.en: During the nineteenth century periodicals multiply, magazines and learned journals included, and the noun settles into its everyday sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪期刊大量涌现，包括杂志与学术刊物，这个名词的日常义由此固定。

note.en: Periodical sits inside the Greek family of periodos and is easily confused with the family of phenomenon; among publications it is close to journal and magazine.
note.cn: periodical 处在希腊语 periodos 的词族之中，很容易与 phenomenon 一族混看；在出版物里，它与 journal 和 magazine 邻近。

entries.definition: recurring at regular intervals
entries.definitionCN: 周期性的；定期的（形容词，无名词义）

entries.definition: at regular intervals
the quality of recurring in cycles
a magazine on a serious subject, often for specialists
entries.definitionCN: 学术性刊物（尤指专业期刊）

entries.definition: a thin publication with articles and pictures
a short bulletin sent to members of a group

normalIntro.en: Periodical is periodos, a going round, plus a suffix that turns a cycle into an object.
normalIntro.cn: periodical 是 periodos（绕行一圈）加上把循环变成具体事物的后缀。

normal.en: Take periodic, add -al, and you gain a noun for the publication itself.
normal.cn: 在 periodic 后面加 -al，就多出指刊物本身的名词义。

normal.en: Peri- means around and hodos means way, so the root is a round trip.
normal.cn: peri- 意为环绕，hodos 意为路，词根就是「绕一圈回来」。

normal.en: A monthly periodical is a clock that hands you a new issue each month.
normal.cn: 月刊就是一只钟，每月准点递来新一期。

normal.en: Periodic stays an adjective; only periodical can be the thing on the shelf.
normal.cn: periodic 只能作形容词；能指架上那本书的只有 periodical。

normal.en: Compare phenomenon: the same letters, but its root is Greek phainein, to show.
normal.cn: 对比 phenomenon：字母相似，但它的词根是希腊语 phainein（显现）。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of matching covers, each dated one month later than the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠同款封面，每一本比上一本晚一个月。

abstract.en: Imagine a reader who climbs the same shelf every thirty days.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者每三十天就登上同一个书架。

abstract.en: Think of a sentence that opens and closes, then is printed again.
abstract.cn: 想一句首尾收口的话，然后被一次一次印出来。

examples.en: She writes reviews for several learned periodicals.
examples.cn: 她为几份学术期刊写评论。

examples.en: The room stores periodicals from the last fifty years.
examples.cn: 这间屋子存放着过去五十年的期刊。

examples.en: Periodical inspections keep the equipment in working order.
examples.cn: 定期检查让设备保持可用状态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮（pe）瑞（ri）奥（o）迪（di）扣（cal）」——想象每期杂志封面都有个按期变换的扣子；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 peri-（环绕）+ hodos（路）→ 希腊语 periodos（绕行一圈、周期）→ 拉丁语 periodus → 英语 periodic（周期的）+ 词尾 -al → periodical（周期性的；期刊），核心义「按时绕回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Periodical starts from the cycle of periodos and grows both an adjective of recurrence and a noun for things that come back on schedule, above all the journal.
sensesIntro.cn: periodical 从 periodos 的「循环」出发，既长出表示反复发生的形容词义，也长出表示按期重来之物的名词义，其中最常用的是期刊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of matching magazines, each one a month newer than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠同款杂志，每本都比上一本晚一个月。

branches.en: The journal that returns each month is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 每月按时回来的期刊是日常义项。

branches.en: Events that come round again take the adjective sense.
branches.cn: 反复重来的事件取形容词义。

branches.en: The name of the class becomes the name of the medium.
branches.cn: 类别的名字转而成为媒介本身的名字。

branches.en: A periodical is periodical because its issues appear periodically.
branches.cn: 期刊之所以叫期刊，是因为它的各期按期出现。

branches.en: The early round-trip route and the modern issue share one circuit.
branches.cn: 早期的环游路线与今天的期刊共用同一个「绕行」意象。

intro.en: Periodical is the adjective periodic with a suffix that both refines the adjective and lets it become a noun. Its family goes back to the Greek parts peri- and hodos.
intro.cn: periodical 是在形容词 periodic 后加一个词尾构成，这个词尾既细化了形容词义，又让它能作名词。它的词族可追溯到希腊语构件 peri- 与 hodos。

latinIntro.en: The Greek parts are peri- around and hodos way; Latin periodus passes the compound on to English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语构件是 peri-（环绕）与 hodos（路）；拉丁语 periodus 把这个复合词传给英语。

items.example: Peri- carries the idea of going round.
items.exampleCN: peri- 带来绕行的意思。

items.example: Hodos supplies the road inside the word.
items.exampleCN: hodos 提供词里的「路」。

items.example: Periodos is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: periodos 是整族的源头。

items.meaning: a circuit, a cycle of time
items.example: Periodus is the form English received.
items.exampleCN: 英语收到的是 periodus 这一形式。

items.example: The suffix -ic builds periodic from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 由名词造出 periodic。

items.meaning: relating to, or a thing of that kind
items.example: The suffix -al forms periodical and lets it stand as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 periodical，并让它能独立作名词。

items.example: Periodic is the adjective without a noun use.
items.exampleCN: periodic 是没有名词义的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds periodically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 periodically。

items.example: The suffix -ity builds periodicity from periodic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 由 periodic 构成 periodicity。

latinEntries.meaning: a circuit, a cycle of time

definition_zh: 外围的；边缘的；周边的；次要的；辅助的
definition_en: situated on the edge of something, or of secondary importance
core_image: 圆心之外的一圈：主体在中央，这个词所指的事物沿着外缘散开
scene: 会议桌上，大家争的正是报告的细枝末节，而真正的核心结论没人提起。At the meeting, everyone argued about peripheral details instead of the main finding.
sceneCN: 这里 peripheral 是「次要的、无关紧要的」（第 5 个义项：地位次要的）；句意：开会时大家争论的都是报告里次要的细节，而不是真正的核心结论。

pos.zh: 外围的；边缘的；周边的；次要的；辅助的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「在外围；次要地」
形容词去后缀 -al 后得到的同根名词，义为「外围；周边」
形容词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使边缘化」

senses.title: Relating to the outer boundary
senses.definition: situated on or relating to the outer edge of an area or object
senses.definitionCN: 位于或关于某片区域、某个物体的外缘的
senses.example: The city has expanded into its peripheral districts.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市已经扩展到它的外围城区。
senses.why: Greek peri means around and pherein means to carry, so the word first points to what is carried around a central line.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 peri 意为「周围」，pherein 意为「携带」，所以这个词首先指沿中心线「绕在外边」的部分。

senses.title: Outside the main area of vision
senses.definition: describing the part of the field of vision away from the centre
senses.definitionCN: 描述视野中偏离中心的区域的
senses.example: A movement in my peripheral vision made me turn.
senses.exampleCN: 余光里有个动静，让我转过头去。
senses.why: The eye is a circle with a sharp centre, and everything beyond it is literally the ring around the centre.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛是一个中间锐利、四周松散的圆，中心之外的一切都真实地处在「圆心外的一圈」上。

senses.title: Auxiliary equipment
senses.definition: used in computing for devices that connect to a main computer
senses.definitionCN: 计算机用语中，指连接到主机的辅助设备
senses.example: The printer is the most used peripheral in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机是办公室里用得最多的外围设备。
senses.why: The computer processor sits at the centre, and the printer or keyboard is the kit hanging on its outer ring.
senses.whyCN: 电脑处理器处在中央，打印机和键盘就是挂在它外圈上的配件。

senses.title: Situated on the margins of an economy
senses.definition: located away from the main centres of population or wealth
senses.definitionCN: 位于人口或财富主要中心之外的
senses.example: Investment is concentrated in the capital, leaving peripheral regions behind.
senses.exampleCN: 投资集中在首都，把边境地区甩在了后面。
senses.why: Economists draw the rich core at the middle and the poorer regions around it, so the outer ring becomes the underdeveloped area.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把富裕的核心画在中间、较穷的地区围在四周，于是外圈就成了欠发达地区。

senses.title: Of minor importance
senses.definition: of secondary importance and not central to the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 重要性居次、不是事情核心的
senses.example: The witness gave only peripheral information to the case.
senses.exampleCN: 这位证人只提供了与案件关系次要的信息。
senses.why: The spatial ring becomes a judgment of value: what is on the edge matters less than what holds the centre.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的「外圈」变成了价值判断：处在边上的东西，不如占据中心的东西重要。

intro.en: Peripheral comes through late Latin from Greek periphereia, the circumference of a circle.
intro.cn: peripheral 经由晚期拉丁语进入英语，源头是希腊语 periphereia，意为圆周。

items.en: Peri means around, and pherein means to carry and later to revolve.
items.cn: peri 意为周围，pherein 意为携带，后来又有运转之意。

items.en: Periphereia means the circumference or the outer line of a circle.
items.cn: periphereia 意为圆周，也就是一个圆的外缘。

items.en: Peripheria keeps the sense of a boundary line drawn around a body.
items.cn: peripheria 保留「围绕某个形体画出的边界线」这一含义。

items.en: Geometry first uses periphery for the outline of a figure.
items.cn: 几何学最先用 periphery 指图形的轮廓。

items.en: The adjective peripheral grows from periphery and spreads into medicine and technology.
items.cn: 形容词 peripheral 由 periphery 派生，并扩展到医学与技术领域。

note.en: Peripheral is the adjective of periphery, close to perimeter and to ordinary words for edges.
note.cn: peripheral 是 periphery 的形容词形式，与 perimeter 以及表示边缘的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: the outer edge of an area
in a secondary or outer way
using a roundabout form of words
entries.definitionCN: 迂回表达的；绕圈子说话的

entries.definition: at or near an edge, of little importance
far from the centre of a place
on the outside of something

normalIntro.en: Peripheral is the adjective built on periphery, so the ring image and the computer image share one root.
normalIntro.cn: peripheral 是由 periphery 构成的形容词，因此圆圈的意象和电脑配件的意象共享同一个根。

normal.en: Greek peri means around and pherein means to carry, so peripheral things are carried around the centre.
normal.cn: 希腊语 peri 意为周围，pherein 意为携带，所以 peripheral 的东西是被绕在中心周围的。

normal.en: A peripheral device such as a mouse or printer sits around the computer itself.
normal.cn: 鼠标、打印机这类外围设备，位置就在电脑主机周围。

normal.en: Peripheral vision is the soft ring of sight outside the sharp centre.
normal.cn: 周边视觉就是锐利中心以外那圈柔和的视野。

normal.en: The opposite is central, and the two words together describe a core and its outer ring.
normal.cn: 它的反义是 central，这两个词合起来描述的正是核心与它周围的外圈。
